answer: Spectral occupancy registration: each identity claims a unique radio band at a fixed location, and a regional coordinator assigns channels by measuring live signal energy at that spot. A claim is accepted only when its measured floor sits below a published ledge, so two identities cannot share one band. An operator physically cannot fake having many separated sites, since transmitters and receivers need real spacing. Each new vertex on the map costs hardware, power, and a site lease. Duplicate signals collapse a reef of channels into one detectable cluster, letting coordinators prune them.
